She works strategically and as a whole, from the first idea to the finished implementation. magazine:1120.text: Stories Photo essay Letter Subscribe Atlas Issue 12 · Winter The slow way north: nine days by train, ferry and foot to the edge of the map. In this issue Seven stories, four countries Alps A village that closes its road for winter Desert Six hundred kilometres of empty road Coast The harbour that paints its boats every spring Rail Sleeping on the night train, and why it is back Nine days north A photo essay by Ines Holm Day one. The road along the cliffs, before anyone else is up. Day four. The night train, somewhere past the border. Day seven. The last village with a shop. Day nine. The end of the line, and the boats. Getting there is the point. The fast way north takes three hours and two airports. We took nine days, and on most of them we did not know where we would sleep. This issue is about the long way round: the night trains coming back, the roads that close for winter, and the people who live at the end of them. A letter from somewhere, every Sunday. One place, one story, a few photographs. No more than that. Email Subscribe Free. Leave any time. Fictional demo, drawn by the Lagoon library. magazine:390.text: Stories Photo essay Letter Subscribe Atlas Issue 12 · Winter The slow way north: nine days by train, ferry and foot to the edge of the map. In this issue Seven stories, four countries Alps A village that closes its road for winter Desert Six hundred kilometres of empty road Coast The harbour that paints its boats every spring Rail Sleeping on the night train, and why it is back Nine days north A photo essay by Ines Holm Day one. The road along the cliffs, before anyone else is up. Day four. The night train, somewhere past the border. Day seven. The last village with a shop. Day nine. The end of the line, and the boats. Getting there is the point. The fast way north takes three hours and two airports. We took nine days, and on most of them we did not know where we would sleep. This issue is about the long way round: the night trains coming back, the roads that close for winter, and the people who live at the end of them. A letter from somewhere, every Sunday. One place, one story, a few photographs. No more than that. Email Subscribe Free. Leave any time. Fictional demo, drawn by the Lagoon library.
